mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-Fed periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher unemployment expectations suppress equity risk premia.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 6.5%, or the effect is absent in high-unemployment periods.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household utilization) above 90% for two months is followed by a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals accelerating consumer demand.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return after the two-month high utilization, or the pattern repeats without effect.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 2% followed by a rise above the prior month's level predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it indicates supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% then rises above previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive and significant when the pattern occurs, or the effect is not detectable in the data.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both show a double-dip in inflation (CPIAUCSL < 233 and then > 233 in two consecutive months) while FEDFUNDS remains below 3%, the S&P 5-day forward return is positive due to expectations of future rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL double-dips below 233 then above 233 while FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not positive or the pattern does not coincide with a positive return in practice.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 130,000 followed by a sustained rise to >140,000 in the next two months predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as labor market recovery strengthens sentiment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 130,000 then rises >2,000 each month for two months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward return when the labor recovery pattern occurs, or the effect is spurious.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 2023Q1 medians predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return as momentum in demand persists.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > median_2023Q1 and RSAFS > median_2023Q1 in two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when both proxies show the pattern, or the effect is not robust across multiple backtests.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in GDPC1 (GDP) followed by a month with GDPC1 above the 2023Q1 median and RSAFS < 300M predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak demand offsets recovery in output.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 down 3 months then up above median while RSAFS < 300M
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive when the pattern occurs, or the interaction is not statistically significant.
